paper: Early prediction of circulatory failure in the intensive care unit using machine learning
authors_short: Hyland SL, Faltys M, Hüser M, et al.
problem: Early warning of circulatory failure in ICU patients
method: Gradient-boosted ML early-warning system integrating multi-organ measurements
data: High-resolution Bern ICU database (240 patient-years; HiRID) with external validation cohort
claimed_novelty: Detects 90% of circulatory-failure events (82% >2 h ahead), AUROC 0.94, with ~0.05 alarms per patient-hour, lower false-alarm rate than threshold systems
what_they_do_not_do: Target is composite circulatory failure (MAP/lactate/vasopressor), not a sustained MAP<65 crossing; supervised black-box model; no closed-form physiological prior
how_ours_differs: We forecast a short-horizon MAP<65 crossing with a training-free first-passage probability and only learn a residual on top, reusing their alarms-per-patient-hour framing.

paper: Prediction of hypotension events with physiologic vital sign signatures in the intensive care unit
authors_short: Yoon JH, Jeanselme V, Dubrawski A, et al.
problem: Predict first hypotension event in ICU 15-60 min ahead
method: Random forest on 30-min windows of minute-level vitals; stacked RF alert model with lockout
data: MIMIC-III minute vitals (1580 hypotensive vs 2279 control stays)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.93 at 15 min; alert system yields 0.79 alerts/subject/hour at 92.4% sensitivity
what_they_do_not_do: Case/control cohort split by event status; no comparison to current or extrapolated MAP; no cross-site transport; only first event
how_ours_differs: We evaluate every actionable time point without case-control sampling and anchor predictions on a closed-form drift-diffusion crossing probability rather than a learned RF score.

paper: Early prediction of hemodynamic interventions in the intensive care unit using machine learning
authors_short: Rahman A, Chang Y, Dong J, et al.
problem: Predict initiation of hemodynamic interventions 1 h ahead (Hemodynamic Stability Index)
method: Ensemble of decision trees with confidence intervals and abstention
data: eICU Research Institute database, 208,375 ICU stays
claimed_novelty: HSI AUC 0.82, beats SBP and shock index; abstains under low confidence; feature attributions
what_they_do_not_do: Label is treatment initiation rather than MAP threshold crossing; hourly resolution; fully data-driven
how_ours_differs: We target minute-scale MAP<65 crossings with an interpretable stochastic baseline and test transport between MIMIC, eICU and VitalDB rather than predicting treatment start.

paper: External validation of a machine learning model to predict hemodynamic instability in intensive care unit
authors_short: Chiang D-H, Tian C, Zeyu J, et al.
problem: Externally validate HSI for haemodynamic instability in an Asian ICU population
method: Application of the HSI decision-tree ensemble; threshold selection and lead-time analysis
data: Taipei Veterans General Hospital, 15,967 ICU patients (2010-2020)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.76 externally, better than shock index and SBP; reports lead time before intervention
what_they_do_not_do: Performance drop on transport is reported but not mitigated; outcome is intervention-based; no physics prior
how_ours_differs: We study transport of a model whose core is training-free, so the anchor component cannot overfit the source site.

paper: Development and validation of a dynamic early warning system with time-varying machine learning models for predicting hemodynamic instability in critical care: a multicohort study
authors_short: Chiang D-H, Jiang Z, Tian C, et al.
problem: Continuous hourly risk of haemodynamic instability in ICU (TvHEWS)
method: Hourly-updating time-varying ML models
data: VGHTPE 2010 and 2022 cohorts plus external MIMIC-IV
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.93 internal, 0.82 on MIMIC-IV, warnings hours before intervention
what_they_do_not_do: Hourly granularity; recall drops to 0.36 on MIMIC-IV; no closed-form forecast of MAP dynamics; alarm burden per patient-hour not the central metric
how_ours_differs: We work at minute resolution on actionable moments and report sensitivity and lead time against alarms per patient-hour across three sources.

paper: A machine-learning approach to predicting hypotensive events in ICU settings
authors_short: Moghadam MC, Abad EMK, Bagherzadeh N, et al.
problem: Real-time prediction of ICU hypotension up to 30 min ahead from 5 min of history
method: Supervised ML classifier with time-resolved evaluation and F1-optimised threshold
claimed_novelty: Accuracy 94%, sensitivity 85%, PPV 81%; 80% of events flagged 25 min early
what_they_do_not_do: No current-MAP or extrapolation baseline; evaluation within 30 min of events rather than all times; single source
how_ours_differs: Like them we use only a few minutes of history, but we turn it into an analytic drift/volatility crossing probability and score all time points, not just pre-event windows.

paper: Predicting hypotension in the ICU using noninvasive physiological signals
authors_short: Moghadam MC, Masoumi E, Kendale S, Bagherzadeh N
problem: ICU hypotension prediction from noninvasive signals
method: ML classifier; noninvasive MAP simulated by down-sampling invasive MAP
claimed_novelty: Shows NIMAP is essential and higher BP sampling frequency improves prediction (sensitivity 84%, PPV 73%)
what_they_do_not_do: No stochastic model of MAP; no cross-site evaluation; no explicit alarm burden
how_ours_differs: We model MAP itself as a drifting diffusion whose volatility estimate naturally depends on sampling, and we test transport across sites.

paper: The Physiological Deep Learner: First application of multitask deep learning to predict hypotension in critically ill patients
authors_short: Cherifa M, Interian Y, Blet A, et al.
problem: Forecast MAP and HR 60 min ahead and derive acute hypotensive episode risk (MAP<65 for 5 min)
method: Multitask deep learning (MTL-PDL) regressing future MAP and HR
data: MIMIC-based development with external validation dataset
claimed_novelty: R2 0.75 for MAP at 60 min; PPV 90% when predicted MAP <=60
what_they_do_not_do: Point forecast of MAP rather than probability of crossing; no uncertainty-to-probability mapping; deep model fully learned
how_ours_differs: We convert a local MAP forecast with explicit volatility into a calibrated crossing probability analytically, and only the residual is learned.

paper: Prediction of an Acute Hypotensive Episode During an ICU Hospitalization With a Super Learner Machine-Learning Algorithm
authors_short: Cherifa M, Blet A, Chambaz A, et al.
problem: Predict acute hypotensive episodes (MAP<65 for >=5 min) 10 min ahead in ICU
method: Super Learner ensemble with Haar-wavelet features from HR, SpO2, ABP plus clinical covariates
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.93 (one random period per patient) / 0.89 (all periods); external validation
what_they_do_not_do: Shows performance depends on sampling of periods but does not correct selection bias; no MAP-only baseline; no first-passage view
how_ours_differs: We share their exact event definition but replace the learned ensemble with a closed-form crossing probability plus residual, evaluated on all actionable moments.

paper: Generalizable deep temporal models for predicting episodes of sudden hypotension in critically ill patients: a personalized approach
authors_short: Chan BW, Chen B, Sedghi A, et al.
problem: Predict patient-specific acute hypotensive episodes 10-60 min ahead
method: Deep temporal models with a personalised AHE definition
claimed_novelty: Personalised AHE label and multi-institution generalisation (AUROC 0.57-0.87)
what_they_do_not_do: Changes the outcome definition rather than the predictor; no interpretable stochastic baseline; no alarm-burden analysis
how_ours_differs: We keep the standard MAP<65/5-min target and gain interpretability from an explicit drift-volatility model instead of redefining the event.

paper: An investigation of patterns in hemodynamic data indicative of impending hypotension in intensive care
authors_short: Lee J, Mark RG
problem: Detect patterns that precede hypotensive episodes 1-2 h ahead in ICU
method: Neural networks for classification and for regression of future MAP using MAP, HR, PP, relative CO features
claimed_novelty: Mean AUROC 0.918; demonstrates discriminative pre-hypotension patterns
what_they_do_not_do: Case/control windows; hour-scale horizons; no probabilistic crossing model
how_ours_differs: We forecast minute-scale crossings using a diffusion model of MAP and avoid case-control window selection.

paper: Forecasting Hypotension during Vasopressor Infusion via Time Series Analysis
authors_short: Shin S, Reisner AT, Yapps B, et al.
problem: Forecast sustained hypotension during vasopressor infusion in ICU
method: Logistic regression and autoregressive (AR) time-series forecasting vs simple threshold detector
claimed_novelty: AR and LR models warn several minutes before sustained hypotension without more false alarms; AR flexible to any threshold
what_they_do_not_do: AR point forecast with no analytic probability of first crossing within a horizon; restricted to vasopressor periods; no ML residual
how_ours_differs: Closest classical statistical competitor: we go beyond AR point forecasting by computing the inverse-Gaussian first-passage probability within H minutes and adding an ML residual.

paper: Towards actionable hypotension prediction -- predicting catecholamine therapy initiation in the intensive care unit
authors_short: Koebe R, Saibel N, Lopez Alcaraz JM, et al.
problem: Predict catecholamine initiation within 15 min in ICU
method: XGBoost with SHAP on 2-h MAP context statistics plus covariates
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.82 vs 0.69 for MAP<65 baseline; reframes target as treatment escalation
what_they_do_not_do: Does not predict MAP crossings; no stochastic baseline; single database
how_ours_differs: We keep MAP<65 as target but supply a physics-anchored probability, and evaluate transport across three databases.

paper: Machine-learning Algorithm to Predict Hypotension Based on High-fidelity Arterial Pressure Waveform Analysis
authors_short: Hatib F, Jian Z, Buddi S, et al.
problem: Predict intraoperative MAP<65 5-15 min ahead (Hypotension Prediction Index)
method: Logistic-type model on 3,022 arterial-waveform features per beat
data: 1,334 retrospective patients for training; 204-patient prospective external cohort
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.95 at 15 min; sensitivity/specificity ~88%/87%
what_they_do_not_do: Case-control sample selection later shown to inflate performance; proprietary; no explicit MAP dynamics
how_ours_differs: We replace the opaque waveform index with a transparent first-passage probability and evaluate without the case-control sampling that inflated HPI.

paper: Deep learning models for the prediction of intraoperative hypotension
authors_short: Lee S, Lee HC, Chu YS, et al.
problem: Real-time IOH prediction 5/10/15 min ahead
method: Deep learning classifiers and MAP regressors on ABP, ECG, PPG, capnography waveforms
claimed_novelty: Multichannel models outperform single-signal; AUROC15 ~0.90 invasive
what_they_do_not_do: Selection of event/non-event samples; no MAP-only comparison; no transport
how_ours_differs: We use only numeric trends, compute a closed-form crossing probability, and test transport from ICU data to VitalDB rather than training on VitalDB waveforms.

paper: Supervised Machine-learning Predictive Analytics for Prediction of Postinduction Hypotension
authors_short: Kendale SM, Kulkarni P, Rosenberg AD, et al.
problem: Predict postinduction hypotension (MAP<55 within 10 min of induction)
method: Several supervised classifiers (GBM best) on EHR, medication, comorbidity and vital-sign features
claimed_novelty: GBM AUROC 0.76 for postinduction hypotension
what_they_do_not_do: Static pre/peri-induction risk, not continuous short-horizon forecasting
how_ours_differs: We provide a continuously updated, horizon-specific crossing probability rather than a one-off induction risk.

paper: Predicting intraoperative hypotension using deep learning with waveforms of arterial blood pressure, electroencephalogram, and electrocardiogram: Retrospective study
authors_short: Jo Y-Y, Jang J-H, Kwon J-m, et al.
problem: IOH prediction 3-15 min ahead
method: Deep networks on ABP, ECG, EEG waveforms
claimed_novelty: ABP+EEG best (AUROC 0.935 at 5 min) and better calibrated
what_they_do_not_do: No unbiased all-time-point evaluation or MAP-only baseline; single centre
how_ours_differs: We test whether a few-parameter diffusion model on MAP numerics already captures most of what waveform deep nets report, under unbiased sampling.

paper: Short-Term Event Prediction in the Operating Room (STEP-OP) of Five-Minute Intraoperative Hypotension Using Hybrid Deep Learning
authors_short: Choe S, Park E, Shin W, et al.
problem: Forecast 5-min IOH from arterial waveforms
method: Weighted ensemble of CNN and RNN (hybrid deep learning)
claimed_novelty: STEP-OP ensemble exceeds single CNN/RNN and logistic regression in AUPRC
what_they_do_not_do: 'Hybrid' means ensemble of neural nets, not mechanistic+ML; no transport; no alarm burden
how_ours_differs: Our hybrid couples a stochastic-process prior with an ML residual, not two neural networks.

paper: Early prediction of intraoperative hypotension: development and validation of the HypoBridCast hybrid deep learning model
authors_short: Wang Y, Zeng X, Chen L, et al.
problem: IOH (MAP<=65 for >=1 min) prediction 5-15 min ahead
method: Conv1D + Transformer on multi-waveform data plus preoperative variables
claimed_novelty: Internal 5-min AUROC 0.94; external evaluation; gains over MAP-only baselines
what_they_do_not_do: Hybrid of neural modules, not physics; requires waveforms; no all-time-point alarm-burden analysis
how_ours_differs: Our 'hybrid' is a closed-form first-passage logit offset plus residual, trained-free at its core and portable to numeric ICU data.

paper: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
authors_short: Chaari N, Winski G, Hallbäck M, et al.
venue: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
problem: Assess reliability and cross-centre generalisation of IOH prediction vs MAP thresholds
method: Deep learning vs MAP threshold; 'Gray Zone' (65-75 mmHg) inclusion; standardised MAP difference between classes
claimed_novelty: Shows inflated performance stems from selection bias; asymmetric cross-centre generalisability
what_they_do_not_do: No stochastic forecast; still a sample-based (not all-time) evaluation; no ICU data
how_ours_differs: We extend their cross-centre bias-aware evaluation to ICU-to-OR transport and add an interpretable diffusion anchor that is strongest exactly in the 65-75 mmHg gray zone.

paper: Frequency Domain Deep Learning With Non-Invasive Features for Intraoperative Hypotension Prediction
authors_short: Moon J-H, Lee G, Lee SM, et al.
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
problem: IOH prediction using non-invasive and invasive biosignals
method: DFT frequency features + time-domain deep learning with interpretable modules
claimed_novelty: Frequency-domain inputs improve AUROC especially for non-invasive data (0.898 vs 0.853)
what_they_do_not_do: Segment-based evaluation; no MAP dynamics model; no transport
how_ours_differs: We exploit MAP trend and volatility in the time domain analytically rather than learning spectral features.

paper: Prediction of intraoperative hypotension using deep learning models based on non-invasive monitoring devices
authors_short: Jeong H, Kim D, Kim DW, et al.
venue: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
problem: IOH (SBP<90) prediction 5 min ahead from non-invasive monitors
method: Attention-based deep networks on NIBP, ECG, PPG, capnography, BIS
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.92 internal, 0.83 external
what_they_do_not_do: Different event definition; external drop not analysed for selection bias; no stochastic baseline
how_ours_differs: We target MAP<65 sustained 5 min with a training-free core whose transport does not require refitting.

paper: Pharmacokinetic State Space Models for Unbiased Prediction of Haemodynamic Collapse
authors_short: Nagaraj R, Chindula S, Das B
venue: arXiv preprint / Lecture Notes in Computer Science
problem: IOH prediction incorporating anaesthetic drug infusion history
method: Mamba state-space deep network with propofol/remifentanil effect-site concentrations; lead-gap filtering
data: Intraoperative data (VitalDB-type; abstract does not name it: UNVERIFIED)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.736; shows unfiltered training learns to detect ongoing rather than future hypotension
what_they_do_not_do: 'State space' is a neural sequence architecture, not a stochastic MAP model; no first-passage probability; no ICU data
how_ours_differs: We share their concern with leakage of ongoing hypotension but restrict to actionable moments and use an explicit stochastic process rather than a Mamba network.

paper: Forecasting cumulative intraoperative hypotension burden: patient-disjoint evaluation of quantile boosting and alert policies
authors_short: Zhao Y
problem: Forecast next-15-min MAP deficit below 65 (burden) and separate forecast skill from alert performance
method: Quantile boosting, direct and residual-on-persistence, vs climatology and persistence; validation-selected alert thresholds
data: VitalDB numeric MAP (10-s medians), subject-disjoint splits
claimed_novelty: Residual quantile boosting beats persistence; shows warning performance depends on alert rule
what_they_do_not_do: Single source; no closed-form stochastic model; residual is relative to persistence not to a diffusion prior; no ICU
how_ours_differs: Close in spirit (residual over a simple MAP baseline, alert-policy evaluation), but our anchor is an analytic first-passage probability and we test ICU-to-OR transport.

paper: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
authors_short: Buré S, Joachim J, Di Meglio F
problem: Choose an individual MAP target and norepinephrine dose to keep risk of MAP<65 below a set limit
method: Reduced PK/PD model fit online; local Gaussian approximation propagates uncertainty to probability of any future MAP<65
data: Retrospective surgical records plus 4,096 virtual patients
claimed_novelty: Probabilistic risk of falling below 65 mmHg drives dose/target selection (6.9% vs 25% hypotension rate)
what_they_do_not_do: Control/dosing rather than early warning; drug-driven PK/PD rather than drift-diffusion of MAP; no ML residual; no ICU
how_ours_differs: Nearest probabilistic competitor: they compute P(MAP<65) from a PK/PD model for dosing, whereas we compute a first-passage probability from local drift/volatility for alarms and add a learned residual.

paper: Performance of the Hypotension Prediction Index May Be Overestimated Due to Selection Bias
authors_short: Enevoldsen J, Vistisen ST
problem: Critique of HPI training/validation data selection
method: Analytical critique with simulated data
claimed_novelty: Shows that HPI's sampling makes MAP<75 always predict hypotension, inflating apparent performance
what_they_do_not_do: Does not propose an alternative predictor
how_ours_differs: We adopt their bias-free evaluation principle and propose a transparent MAP-dynamics predictor to fill the gap they identified.

paper: Ability of an Arterial Waveform Analysis-Derived Hypotension Prediction Index to Predict Future Hypotensive Events in Surgical Patients
authors_short: Davies SJ, Vistisen ST, Jian Z, et al.
problem: Validate HPI vs other haemodynamic variables
method: Retrospective ROC analysis of HPI and haemodynamic variables
claimed_novelty: HPI AUROC 0.93/0.90/0.88 at 5/10/15 min, reportedly superior to MAP
what_they_do_not_do: Uses backward case-control style analysis later questioned; superiority over MAP later corrected
how_ours_differs: We evaluate forward on all time points where the MAP-superiority claim is known to vanish.

paper: Is Continuous Intraoperative Monitoring of Mean Arterial Pressure as Good as the Hypotension Prediction Index Algorithm?: Research Letter
authors_short: Mulder MP, Harmannij-Markusse M, Donker DW, et al.
problem: Compare HPI signal and alarms with MAP
method: Cross-correlation of HPI and MAP; alarm concordance
data: 33 high-risk noncardiac surgery patients, unselected 20-s data
claimed_novelty: HPI strongly mirrors MAP in unselected data
what_they_do_not_do: Pilot only; no new predictor
how_ours_differs: We start from their finding that MAP dominates and add the missing ingredient, MAP trend and volatility, in a probabilistic form.

paper: Hypotension Prediction Index Is Equally Effective in Predicting Intraoperative Hypotension during Noncardiac Surgery Compared to a Mean Arterial Pressure Threshold: A Prospective Observational Study
authors_short: Mulder MP, Harmannij-Markusse M, Fresiello L, et al.
problem: Compare HPI with MAP-based predictors
method: Prospective observational; alarm agreement and ROC of HPI vs MAP, linearly extrapolated MAP, delta MAP
claimed_novelty: HPI AUROC 0.89 vs MAP 0.88; MAP 72-73 mmHg threshold matches HPI alarms
what_they_do_not_do: Does not try a stochastic forecast; extrapolated MAP did worse than current MAP
how_ours_differs: We test whether a noise-aware drift model beats current MAP where naive linear extrapolation failed.

paper: Comparison of Differences in Cohort (Forward) and Case Control (Backward) Methodologic Approaches for Validation of the Hypotension Prediction Index
authors_short: Davies SJ, Sessler DI, Jian Z, et al.
problem: Quantify impact of forward vs backward validation on HPI
method: Re-analysis of pooled studies with both methodologies
claimed_novelty: HPI AUC remains ~0.92 in forward analysis; MAP itself has similar AUC (~0.93)
what_they_do_not_do: Industry-affiliated; still threshold/ROC focused; no alarm-burden or ICU evaluation
how_ours_differs: We adopt forward, all-time evaluation and report alarm burden, which their ROC analysis omits.

paper: Comparing the Hypotension Prediction Index to Mean Arterial Pressure and Linear Extrapolated Mean Arterial Pressure for the Prediction of Intraoperative Hypotension: A Secondary Analysis
authors_short: Massari D, de Keijzer IN, Vos JJ
problem: Head-to-head HPI vs MAP vs linearly extrapolated MAP
method: Secondary analysis of a mixed-methods cohort
claimed_novelty: HPI not superior to MAP or extrapolated MAP
what_they_do_not_do: Linear extrapolation ignores noise; no probabilistic model
how_ours_differs: Our first-passage probability is the noise-aware generalisation of the linear-extrapolation baseline they tested.

paper: The hypotension prediction index versus mean arterial pressure in predicting intraoperative hypotension: A clinical perspective
authors_short: Rellum SR, Noteboom SH, van der Ster BJP, et al.
problem: Clinical comparison of HPI vs MAP alert thresholds
method: Time-to-event, PPV and missed events for HPI popups vs MAP 70-75 alerts
claimed_novelty: HPI gains <1 min lead time over MAP-70 alerts; MAP-75 lowers PPV
what_they_do_not_do: No forecasting model; trade-off framed per alert threshold only
how_ours_differs: We present the same lead-time/PPV trade-off as alarm-burden curves for a probabilistic forecaster.

paper: Prediction of intraoperative hypotension from the linear extrapolation of mean arterial pressure
authors_short: Jacquet-Lagrèze M, Larue A, Guilherme E, et al.
problem: Test linearly extrapolated MAP (LepMAP) for IOH prediction
method: Linear extrapolation of minute MAP vs delta MAP; ROC
claimed_novelty: LepMAP AUC 0.87/0.81/0.69 at 1/2/5 min, far better than delta MAP
what_they_do_not_do: Deterministic extrapolation without volatility; degrades quickly with horizon
how_ours_differs: We keep the drift idea of LepMAP but add volatility and compute the probability of first crossing within the horizon.

paper: The effect of selection bias on the performance of a deep learning-based intraoperative hypotension prediction model using real-world samples from a publicly available database
authors_short: Yang H-L, Celi LA, Lee H, et al.
problem: Quantify selection-bias effect on DL and MAP-only IOH models
method: Train/test DL vs MAP-only on biased vs unbiased sampling; alarms per hour and PPV
claimed_novelty: Unbiased testing: 18.1 alarms/h and PPV 0.068 vs 10.8/h and 0.937 biased; DL gain over MAP not clinically meaningful
what_they_do_not_do: No new predictor; single dataset; no ICU
how_ours_differs: We adopt their unbiased sampling and alarms-per-hour metric and ask whether a physics-anchored model narrows the clinically meaningless gap they found.

paper: Predicting arterial pressure without prejudice: towards effective hypotension prediction models
authors_short: Vistisen ST, Elbers P
problem: Editorial on selection bias in hypotension prediction
method: Commentary on Yang et al.
claimed_novelty: Argues unbiased training lets models learn only modestly beyond current BP; bias inflates PPV
what_they_do_not_do: No empirical method
how_ours_differs: Our study is a direct attempt at the 'unbiased' predictor they call for, with explicit MAP dynamics.

paper: Threshold Regression for Survival Analysis: Modeling Event Times by a Stochastic Process Reaching a Boundary
authors_short: Lee M-LT, Whitmore GA
problem: Model event times as first hitting time of a latent process
method: First-hitting-time (Wiener process / inverse Gaussian) threshold regression with covariates
claimed_novelty: Unifies first-hitting-time survival models with regression structure
what_they_do_not_do: No vital-sign or real-time forecasting application
how_ours_differs: We apply the Wiener first-hitting-time machinery in real time to observed MAP with locally estimated drift and volatility.

paper: A Sequential Bayesian Updated Wiener Process Model for Remaining Useful Life Prediction
authors_short: Li T, Pei H, Pang Z, et al.
problem: Remaining-useful-life prediction for degrading components
method: Wiener process with random drift, sequential Bayesian drift updating, first-passage RUL
claimed_novelty: Sequential Bayesian update uses full degradation history
what_they_do_not_do: Engineering domain; no physiology
how_ours_differs: We transfer the Wiener first-passage RUL logic to MAP 'degradation' toward 65 mmHg with a short sliding window.

paper: Recurrent events modeling based on a reflected Brownian motion with application to hypoglycemia
authors_short: Xie Y, Fu H, Huang Y, et al.
problem: Model hypoglycaemic events as lower-boundary crossings of glucose
method: Reflected Brownian motion with frailty; Bayesian MCMC
claimed_novelty: Boundary-crossing framework for a clinical physiological threshold
what_they_do_not_do: Offline population inference, not bedside early warning; glucose not BP
how_ours_differs: Closest clinical first-passage analogue, but we use it for online, minute-level hypotension warnings with an ML residual.

paper: Bayesian analysis of ambulatory blood pressure dynamics with application to irregularly spaced sparse data
authors_short: Lu Z, Chow S-M, Sherwood A, Zhu H
problem: Model ambulatory BP dynamics
method: Dual nonlinear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SDE with covariates; Bayesian Brownian-bridge sampler
data: Duke Behavioral Investigation of Hypertension Study
claimed_novelty: SDE model of BP surge/dipping with covariate effects
what_they_do_not_do: No threshold-crossing probabilities; ambulatory not acute care
how_ours_differs: We use a simpler local drift-diffusion for acute MAP and compute closed-form crossing probabilities for alarms.

paper: Parity-Skeleton First-Passage Dynamics and Optimal Intervention in Two-Sided Discrete Monitoring Systems
authors_short: Liang Y
problem: First-passage risk for two-sided threshold monitoring and intervention scheduling
method: Biased random walk with absorbing barriers; drift/variance matched from rolling increments; compared to inverse-Gaussian benchmark
data: Synthetic, incl. a synthetic remote-patient-monitoring example
claimed_novelty: Exact finite-horizon crossing risk and ageing properties; links to intervention schedules
what_they_do_not_do: No real clinical data; no hypotension; no ML
how_ours_differs: Methodologically nearest first-passage work, but we validate inverse-Gaussian crossing probabilities on real MAP data across three cohorts.

paper: Short-term vital parameter forecasting in the intensive care unit: A benchmark study leveraging data from patients after cardiothoracic surgery
authors_short: Hinrichs N, Roeschl T, Lanmüeller P, et al.
problem: Benchmark forecasting of six ICU vitals 5-120 min ahead
method: Naive, Theta, ETS, ARIMA, AR-NN, N-BEATS, N-HiTS, GRU, Transformer
claimed_novelty: GRU best; neural models beat statistical ones increasingly with horizon
what_they_do_not_do: Point forecasts; no event probabilities or alarms
how_ours_differs: We turn short-horizon MAP forecasting into calibrated crossing probabilities and alarm-burden curves.

paper: A transformer-based diffusion probabilistic model for heart rate and blood pressure forecasting in Intensive Care Unit
authors_short: Chang P, Li H, Quan SF, et al.
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
problem: Probabilistic forecasting of HR, SBP, DBP in ICU
method: Transformer-based denoising diffusion probabilistic model (TDSTF)
claimed_novelty: Better CRPS/MSE and faster inference than baselines
what_they_do_not_do: 'Diffusion' is a generative DL model, not a physical diffusion of MAP; no threshold-crossing alarms
how_ours_differs: We use a physical drift-diffusion with closed-form first-passage probability instead of a generative neural sampler.

paper: Alarm Fatigue: A Patient Safety Concern
authors_short: Sendelbach S, Funk M
problem: Clinical alarm fatigue
method: Narrative review
claimed_novelty: 72-99% of clinical alarms are false; outlines mitigation strategies
what_they_do_not_do: No predictive model
how_ours_differs: We make alarm burden a primary endpoint of a hypotension warning model.

paper: Insights into the Problem of Alarm Fatigue with Physiologic Monitor Devices: A Comprehensive Observational Study of Consecutive Intensive Care Unit Patients
authors_short: Drew BJ, Harris P, Zègre-Hemsey JK, et al.
problem: Quantify ICU monitor alarm burden
method: Annotated observational study of all monitor alarms
claimed_novelty: 187 audible alarms per bed per day; 88.8% arrhythmia alarms false
what_they_do_not_do: No predictive alarms
how_ours_differs: We benchmark predictive alerts in alarms per patient-hour against this baseline burden.

paper: Why the C-statistic is not informative to evaluate early warning scores and what metrics to use
authors_short: Romero-Brufau S, Huddleston JM, Escobar GJ, et al.
problem: Metrics for early warning scores
method: Methodological commentary
claimed_novelty: Recommends sensitivity plus PPV/number-needed-to-evaluate or alert rate instead of AUROC
what_they_do_not_do: No model
how_ours_differs: We report sensitivity vs alerts per patient-hour as they recommend rather than headline AUROC.

paper: Continuous Evaluation Frameworks for Retrospective Evaluation of Clinical Machine Learning Models
authors_short: Natarajan A, Chang Y, McLaverty BP, et al.
problem: Evaluate continuously running clinical ML models
method: Zone-based, PAMC-curve-based and notification-based frameworks
data: Sepsis model predictions on two public datasets

paper: Multi-source data integration through pooling and transfer learning improves generalizability and specialization of deep learning models for ICU mortality and length of stay prediction: a four-database external validation study

method: TPC architecture; single-source vs pooling vs transfer learning

paper: Predicting sepsis using deep learning across international sites: a retrospective development and validation study

paper: Cross-site transportability of an explainable artificial intelligence model for acute kidney injury prediction

paper: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories
